Name: New Carthage, Hub of Iberia: Headland Defenses and the Lagoon Fortress
RagShortTexts: New Carthage has a deep harbor surrounded by water on three sides and a fortress guarded by a narrow isthmus
The shallow lagoon north of the city drains with the tide, giving Scipio an opening to wade across and strike by surprise
As the capital of the Barcid dominion in Iberia, it held vast silver ingots, hostages and military supplies
BaseText: New Carthage (town_wre_carthagonova, modern Cartagena) was founded by Hasdrubal Barca in 228 BC as the administrative capital and main military supply base of Barcid rule over the Iberian Peninsula. The city sits on a peninsula deep inside a natural deep-water bay of the Mediterranean, with the sea to the south, a long narrow channel to the east and a calm, shallow lagoon to the north. It is joined to the land only by a narrow isthmus on the east, an extremely strong position. Inside stood the grand palace of the Barca family, an arsenal, granaries and a treasury storing the output of the silver mines of Castulo, and more than three hundred noble hostages from the native Iberian tribes were held there. In 209 BC the young Scipio waded across the lagoon at low tide and took the city, a legendary surprise attack that turned the tide of the war.

Variants.Content: New Carthage is the heart of the Barca family in Europe. Here are gathered tens of thousands of suits of armor, fine horses and endless silver, and any army that dreams of storming it from the land will be buried outside the isthmus.

The tide of the lagoon is the divine guide to breaking the city, given to Rome by the sea god Neptune! Taking New Carthage not only captured the enemy's treasury but brought all the tribes of Spain over to the Senate.

Our young lords and princesses were held as hostages by the Carthaginians deep in the palace of this stone city. When the Roman legions burst through the gates, the tribes at last broke the chains that bound them.
